explanations: luna: The source dictionary describes the sky as what is above and shelters; 2:22 calls it a structure (السماء بناء) over the earth in its account of provision and creation. | terra: Allah makes the sky a canopy over people. This is a direct Qur'anic instance of the source's dictionary sense of sama as what is above and gives cover.
terra: Allah shades the Children of Israel with clouds. The overhead cloud makes the source's “what rises above and shades” definition tangible.

luna: The verse says east and west belong to Allah and wherever people turn is His face (فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله); it parallels Abraham turning his face to the Creator after seeing heavenly bodies, while its own setting concerns direction of prayer. | terra: East and west belong to Allah, and wherever one turns is Allah's face. It resonates with Abraham's turning his face to the Creator rather than to a rising body on the horizon.

luna: The fasting instruction begins with dawn becoming distinguishable and ends the fast at night; it gives a concrete human boundary for the daylight interval that the section defines through the sun’s course.

luna: The section develops the rising crescent and lunar stations; 2:189 calls the الأهلة time markers (مواقيت) for people and pilgrimage, making the crescent a calendar sign. | terra: The new crescents are appointed measures of time for people and pilgrimage. It directly gives the hilal its practical timekeeping role rather than a divine status.

luna: In Abraham’s argument about lordship, the challenge فأت بها من المغرب turns the sun’s rising from the east into evidence against the ruler who disputes God; the luminary’s course belongs to the Creator. | terra: Abraham answers the claimant of lordship by saying Allah brings the sun from the east and challenging him to bring it from the west. The solar horizon becomes evidence against a false lord.
terra: Allah causes night to enter day and day to enter night while holding dominion. It supplies another direct formulation of the daily transition as sovereign action.

terra: Jesus says Allah is his Lord and their Lord, then commands worship of Him as a straight path. This gives another explicit worship-and-straightness formulation relevant to the source's solar-worship contrast.

luna: The verse pairs creation of the heavens and earth with the succession of night and day (اختلاف الليل والنهار); it presents the section’s turning sky as a sign for reflection. | terra: The creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for people of understanding. It states the reflective frame for the section's whole sky image.
luna: The verse praises Allah as creator of the heavens and earth and maker of darkness and light; it concretizes the section’s al-ʿālam dictionary gloss as a created cosmic and luminous order.

luna: Before the kingdom-of-heaven scene and celestial test, Abraham asks his father whether he takes idols as gods and calls his people clearly astray; this is the narrative prelude to the specific star, moon, and sun test in 6:76–78.

luna: Immediately before the star test, God shows Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and earth (ملكوت السماوات والأرض); this supplies the celestial setting for 6:76 and locates it within God’s display. | terra: Before Abraham's observations of the setting lights, this ayah says he was shown the dominion of the heavens and earth; it supplies the cosmic frame in which the following star, moon, and sun are judged as creatures.

luna: In Abraham’s test of celestial lights, the star sets (أفل), and he says لا أحب الآفلين; a visible light’s disappearance defeats treating it as Lord. | terra: Abraham sees a star and calls it his lord only within the test of its setting; “those that set” cannot be loved as lord. It begins the section's contrast between a visible heavenly light and the true Lord.

luna: Abraham watches the moon set, then says لئن لم يهدني ربي لأكونن من القوم الضالين; this passage itself gathers Rab, guidance, and the lost people named in the section’s Fatiha reading. | terra: The moon rises and then sets; Abraham says that without his Lord's guidance he would belong to the astray people. This directly joins the lunar scene to the source's Rab, hidayah, and dallin language.

luna: Abraham calls the rising sun “greater,” but when it sets (أفلت) he disavows the objects they associate with God; the same test now uses the sun. | terra: The sun rises, is called the larger heavenly body, then sets; Abraham disavows association. It is the source's fullest solar reversal of treating a rising light as divine.

luna: After the sun sets, Abraham turns his face to the One who created the heavens and earth (فطر السماوات والأرض); this gives the section’s worship distinction its creator, rather than a heavenly light, as its object. | terra: Abraham turns his face toward the Originator of the heavens and earth as a hanif. It supplies the positive direction after the star, moon, and sun have proved unfit as objects of devotion.

luna: After Abraham turns to the Creator in 6:79, this verse says his people dispute with him and he answers that Allah has guided him; its own contribution continues the section’s Abraham-and-guidance scene into the people’s challenge. | terra: After the celestial argument, Abraham says that Allah has guided him and that he does not fear the things his people associate with Him. Its own contribution is the passage's explicit contrast between guidance and feared false associates.

luna: Abraham asks how he should fear the partners his people associate with God when they do not fear associating without authority; it continues the same argument after the celestial test and sharpens the rejection of worshiping created things. | terra: Abraham asks why he should fear their associates when they do not fear associating with Allah without authority. It carries the preceding sun-and-moon rejection into a direct argument against association.

luna: The next verse says those who believe without mixing faith with injustice have security and are guided (وهم مهتدون); in Abraham’s argument this answers the section’s fear of becoming among the astray with a stated condition for guidance. | terra: The conclusion of Abraham's exchange gives security and guidance to those whose faith is not mixed with wrongdoing. It supplies the passage's answer to the source's danger of becoming among the astray.

luna: This verse joins dawn splitting, night as rest, and sun and moon by calculation (حسبانا); it makes the section’s day and luminaries part of an ordered time system. | terra: The splitter of dawn makes night for rest and the sun and moon for calculation. It gathers daybreak, the daily rhythm, and celestial measurement into one created order.

luna: The verse says God made stars so people can find their way through land and sea darkness; it gives the star from Abraham’s scene a created navigational role, distinct from treating a heavenly light as Lord or from the section’s spiritual guidance. | terra: Allah makes stars so people can find their way through the darkness of land and sea. It distinguishes their created navigational guidance from the Lord's guidance sought by Abraham.
terra: Allah calls His way straight and commands following it rather than divergent ways. It sharpens the path boundary that 27:24 says solar worship breaches.
terra: Abraham's Lord has guided him to a straight, upright religion. It connects the source's Ibrahim scene to the mustaqim/Q-W-M family without making the noon sense into a further doctrine.

luna: After describing creation of heaven and earth and night covering day, the verse says sun, moon, and stars are subjected to God’s command; their celestial motion is created service, not a reason to worship them. | terra: Allah creates the heavens and earth, covers day with night in rapid pursuit, and makes sun, moon, and stars subject to His command. It supplies the daily sky as an ordered act of lordship.
terra: In the division of Israel into tribes, Allah shades them with the cloud. This repeats the overhanging sheltering scene in a distinct passage.
terra: The mountain is raised over Israel like a canopy as they fear it falling. It is a threatening reversal of the source's sky-as-overhead-cover image.

luna: This verse identifies the Creator and governor of the heavens and earth and commands worship of Him; its own claim anchors the sun and moon’s calculated courses in 10:5 to the Creator rather than to the luminaries.

luna: This verse names the sun’s radiance, the moon’s light, and its stations (منازل) for counting years and حساب; it directly supplies the timekeeping purpose behind the section’s lunar-mansion image. | terra: Allah makes the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and apportions the moon's stations for years and reckoning. This is the section's moon-mansion and measured-time image in Qur'anic form.

luna: The succession of night and day and what God created in the heavens and earth are signs; this directly links the image’s daily sky cycle to its encompassing celestial sphere. | terra: The alternation of night and day and what Allah creates in the heavens and earth are signs for the mindful. It explicitly joins temporal alternation to the populated sky.
terra: Allah makes night for rest and day for seeing. It gives the day/night sky distinct human functions alongside the source's measured lights.

luna: The verse places prayer at the day’s two ends and near parts of the night; it maps worship onto the daylight interval whose middle the section identifies with noon. | terra: Prayer is commanded at the two ends of the day and in approaches of the night. It divides the source's sun-bounded day into acts of worship.

luna: Joseph’s dream shows the sun, moon, and stars prostrating to him, reversing the human prostration to the sun in the Sheba report; 12:100 identifies the scene as a dream fulfilled through his family, so the parallel is symbolic. | terra: In Joseph's dream, the sun, moon, and eleven stars are the ones prostrating. As a dream image, it reverses the direction of solar and lunar prostration in the source's worship contrast.

luna: Joseph says this scene fulfills his earlier dream; his parents and brothers bow to him, clarifying that the sun and moon bowing in 12:4 are dream symbols for family, not worshiped celestial bodies.

luna: The verse says God raised the heavens and subjected sun and moon, each running to a stated term; it directly places the section’s lights under the Creator’s rule. | terra: After raising the heavens, Allah subjects sun and moon, each running to a fixed term. It joins the overhead sky to the finite courses of its two most visible lights.

luna: The verse says created shadows prostrate to God at morning and evening (ظلالهم بالغدو والآصال); against human prostration to the sun, even the image’s changing shade is placed in submission to God. | terra: The shadows of those in the heavens and earth prostrate morning and evening. It gives the changing length and direction of shadow a cosmic posture toward Allah.

luna: The verse says sun and moon are subjected in their continuous courses and night and day are subjected too; it joins the section’s two celestial lights to its full daily cycle. | terra: The sun and moon are made constantly serviceable, as are night and day. It gives the daily cycle the character of provision rather than deity.
terra: Allah places constellations in the sky and beautifies it for observers. It fills the source's sky sphere with visible created markers, including the kind of star Abraham sees.

luna: Night, day, sun, moon, and stars are all subjected by God’s command; this repeats the section’s sky scene while identifying the lights as governed signs. | terra: Allah subjects night, day, sun, moon, and stars, calling them signs for people who understand. It treats the image's lights as intelligible signs under command.

luna: After mentioning landmarks, the verse says people are guided by the stars (وبالنجم هم يهتدون); the stars that appear in Abraham’s test can guide travel without being objects of worship, while Fatiha asks God for guidance. | terra: Landmarks and stars guide travelers. This gives a concrete celestial counterpart to the source's straight-path language without equating physical navigation with salvation.

luna: The source’s q-w-m gloss pictures noon with almost no shadow to right or left; 16:48 depicts shadows inclining on both sides (عن اليمين والشمائل), a specific contrast within the day’s movement. | terra: The shadows of all created things turn right and left in prostration to Allah. Their directional motion contrasts with the source's balanced noon shadow and turns that scene toward worship.

luna: After 16:48’s moving shadows prostrate to God, this verse says all creatures in heaven and earth and the angels prostrate to Him; it widens the same submission scene beyond shadows. | terra: Continuing the moving-shadow image, creatures in the heavens and earth and the angels prostrate to Allah. It widens 16:48's visual prostration into an explicit cosmic worship scene.
terra: Allah makes shades from what He has created and shelters in the mountains. It gives a concrete beneficent instance of the source's secondary sama sense: what is above can give shade.

luna: The verse makes night and day two signs, the day visible for seeking provision, and their sequence a means to count years and calculation; it concretizes the section’s yawm as measurable daylight. | terra: Allah makes night and day two signs so people may seek bounty and know the count of years and reckoning. It supplies a day-and-night counterpart to the moon's measured calendar.

luna: Prayer begins at the sun’s decline (لدلوك الشمس) and continues to night, with dawn named separately; this marks the daily course around the section’s noon sun. | terra: Prayer is set from the sun's decline until night darkness, with the dawn recitation. It maps worship across the changing solar day rather than toward the heavenly body.

luna: The cave passage stages the sun shifting away at rising and setting (تزاور … تقرضهم), then says من يهد الله فهو المهتد; it joins the image’s moving sunlight to its guidance theme. | terra: At sunrise the sun inclines away from the cave to the right, and at sunset passes them on the left; the ayah ends by naming Allah's guidance. It joins directional shadow to the source's straight way and hidayah.
luna: The cave scene continues by saying the young men are asleep and turned from side to side; it supplies the occupants’ condition after 18:17 describes sunlight shifting away from their cave.

luna: Dhul-Qarnayn reaches the setting place of the sun (مغرب الشمس); the scene gives a second concrete horizon image for the section’s daylight span from sunrise to sunset. | terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn reaches the place of sunset and sees the sun setting at a spring. It gives the source's sunset boundary a concrete horizon scene, while remaining a traveler's observation.

luna: Dhul-Qarnayn reaches the rising place of the sun (مطلع الشمس), pairing with 18:86 and the section’s sunrise-to-sunset definition of yawm. | terra: At the place of sunrise, Dhu al-Qarnayn finds a people for whom Allah has made no shelter from it. The exposed rising sun reverses the source's secondary image of what is overhead giving shade.
terra: Jesus declares Allah his Lord and their Lord and says to worship Him; that is a straight path. It repeats the same concrete relation between exclusive worship and the path.
terra: Addressing Israel, Allah recalls shading them with clouds. It preserves the same provided overhead cover within a direct divine address.

luna: The command to glorify God before sunrise and before sunset (قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها) places worship at the two boundaries of the section’s sun-defined day. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord before sunrise and before sunset. It brackets the source's day by its solar limits and directs speech to the Lord rather than the sun.

luna: The section’s dictionary gloss defines the sky as what is above and shelters; 21:32 calls the sky a protected ceiling (سقفا محفوظا), a close Qur’anic image of that covering. | terra: Allah makes the sky a protected ceiling. It develops the image of the overhead sky as a made enclosure rather than an object of reverence.

luna: The verse names night, day, sun, and moon and says each swims in an orbit (فلك); it supplies the moving celestial order behind the image of a sky turning through the day. | terra: Allah creates night, day, sun, and moon, each swimming in an orbit. This is a compact account of the celestial sphere and its moving contents.

luna: The verse explicitly lists الشمس والقمر among those who prostrate to Allah; it reverses the human act of prostrating to the sun in the section. | terra: The sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and creatures prostrate to Allah. It reverses solar and lunar worship: the heavenly bodies belong among those bowing to their Creator.
terra: The ayah says that a day with Allah is like a thousand years of human counting. It marks a deliberate boundary to the source's lexical daylight sense of yawm.
terra: Allah causes night to enter day and day to enter night. Its own contribution is to ground that visible alternation in the hearing and seeing Lord.
terra: Allah holds the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. It makes the overhead heaven dependent on the Creator rather than an independent power.
terra: Allah alternates night and day, calling this a lesson for people of sight. The ayah explicitly makes the visual change in the sky an occasion for perception.
terra: The verse names the time when people put aside clothes at noon, between dawn and night privacy times. It is a direct human-time marker for the source's midday moment.

luna: The source’s q-w-m dictionary image says the noon sun stands overhead while the shadow nearly disappears; 25:45 instead describes shadow extended and the sun as its دليل, giving the changing shadow that makes the noon image perceptible. | terra: Allah extends the shadow and makes the sun its indicator. This directly clarifies the source's noon image by showing shadow's dependence on the sun.

luna: The next verse says God draws the shadow back gradually (قبضناه … قبضا يسيرا); after 25:45’s sun-as-guide, it completes the shadow’s motion around the section’s near-shadowless noon. | terra: The next ayah says the extended shadow is then withdrawn gradually. Its own contribution is the temporal change in shadow that gives the nearly shadowless zenith its place in a larger daily movement.

luna: After the shadow passage, the verse pairs night as a covering with day as renewed activity (الليل لباسا … النهار نشورا); it carries the sun-and-shadow sequence into the other half of the section’s day cycle. | terra: Allah makes night a covering, sleep a rest, and day for waking activity. It adds a human rhythm to the source's passage from celestial light to darkness.

luna: This verse places constellations in the sky together with a lamp and a shining moon; it concretely fills the section’s dictionary image of the sky as a sphere and what it contains. | terra: Allah places constellations in the sky and makes there a lamp and a luminous moon. It presents the sky's visible lights as things He made and placed.

luna: The verse makes night and day succeed one another (خلفة) for remembrance or gratitude; it names the recurring cycle that surrounds the section’s noon and daylight. | terra: Allah makes night and day succeed one another for whoever wishes to remember or give thanks. It turns the source's revolving daily sky into a sequence calling for response to Allah.

luna: The verse just before the sun-worship report says a woman rules the people (امرأة تملكهم); it adds the specific political setting that the section notes for 27:24. | terra: This ayah identifies the ruler as a woman governing the people. Its own contribution is the particular detail that the source places immediately before the report of that people's solar worship.

luna: The source dictionary’s sun-name الإلاهة is tied to worship; the Hudhud reports people سجود للشمس من دون الله and says this held them from السبيل, joining the image’s sun cult to Fatiha’s path and guidance. | terra: The hoopoe finds her people prostrating to the sun apart from Allah, and says they have been turned from the path and are not guided. It directly binds solar worship to the loss of the way.

luna: Following 27:24’s sun worship, the Hudhud asks them to سجود to Allah, who brings forth the hidden in the heavens and earth; the neighbour completes the contrast by naming the rightful recipient of prostration. | terra: Continuing the same report, it says prostration belongs to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and earth. It states the Creator-directed alternative to the people's prostration to the sun.

luna: After the Hudhud’s report and call to prostrate to Allah, this verse says Allah alone is God and Lord of the great throne; it completes the report’s contrast between the sun and its Lord. | terra: The continuation declares that Allah alone is God and Lord of the magnificent throne. In the solar-worship passage, it completes the report's shift from the queen's people to the One they should worship.

luna: In the same report of a sun-worshiping people, Solomon’s letter begins with بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم, repeating the Fatiha’s opening formula and bringing the section’s Bism and Allah features into the solar-cult passage.

luna: The next line of Solomon’s letter tells the queen not to exalt herself and to come as a submitter; in its political setting this is a concrete response to the people’s sun worship, though the command itself is a ruler’s ultimatum.

luna: In the same Queen of Sheba report, this verse says her prior worship besides Allah had held her back; it makes the solar-cult report personal to the ruler and states the barrier that the section associates with being kept from the path.

luna: After the glass-floor scene, the queen says she has wronged herself and submits with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds; this completes the solar-worship report with a specific turn to the Creator. | terra: The queen finally says she submits with Solomon to the Lord of the worlds. It is the narrative resolution of the woman's earlier solar worship, though the ayah itself no longer names the sun.

terra: The rhetorical question asks who guides people through the darknesses of land and sea and whether there is any deity with Allah. It is a nonstellar parallel to the source's created celestial guidance and exclusive lordship.
terra: Allah makes night for rest and day for sight. It assigns the daily sky's two conditions human purposes, echoing the source's definition of day.
terra: If Allah made night continuous, no god other than Him could bring light. The rhetorical question denies a rival ilah the power over the celestial light that sun worship would assume.
terra: If Allah made day continuous, no god other than Him could bring night for rest. It supplies the reciprocal boundary of the daily cycle and sole divine control of it.
terra: From mercy Allah makes night for rest and day for seeking bounty. It gives the day-and-night rhythm a provided function rather than independent power.

luna: Asked who created the heavens and earth and subjected sun and moon, the people answer Allah; the passage makes the worshiped luminary answer to its Creator. | terra: Those questioned acknowledge that Allah created the heavens and earth and subjected sun and moon. The verse exposes the inconsistency of recognizing the Creator while directing devotion elsewhere.
terra: Praise is directed to Allah in the evening, morning, late afternoon, and at noon. It gives the daily stations, including the source's noon, a worshipful response.
luna: The verse names praise to God at evening and when people enter noon (حين تظهرون); it makes noon, where the section’s sun stands overhead, a time of worship directed to God.
terra: Among Allah's signs, heaven and earth stand by His command. Its standing language from the Q-W-M family makes a restrained cosmic parallel to the source's upright sun and balanced day.

luna: The verse describes night entering day and day entering night, then sun and moon running to a term; it expands the image from noon to the alternating cycle that contains it. | terra: Allah merges night into day and day into night and subjects sun and moon for an appointed term. It describes the transition around the day the source defines from sunrise to sunset.
terra: Allah directs the affair from heaven to earth, then it rises to Him in a day measured as a thousand human years. It combines the source's sky with a non-solar scale of yawm.

luna: Night and day enter one another while sun and moon run to a stated term; the verse presents the section’s celestial lights as bounded parts of God’s order. | terra: Allah inserts night into day and day into night, and subjects sun and moon, each moving to a fixed term. It makes the image's alternation and celestial timing acts of Allah.
terra: Shade and scorching heat are declared unequal. This sharpens the source's nearly absent noon shadow by setting shade against the sun's burning opposite.
terra: Night is stripped from day and people are left in darkness. It makes the section's turning daily sky a visible transition rather than a static backdrop.

luna: The verse says the sun runs to its appointed course (لمستقر لها); the visible sun in the section’s day-long sky is itself moving within a measured limit. | terra: The sun runs toward its fixed course by the decree of the Mighty, Knowing. Its movement answers the image of the sun at midday and its later descent with a measured course.

luna: The verse says the moon was measured in stations (منازل) until it returns like an old date stalk; this gives the crescent and the section’s named lunar mansion a visible phase cycle. | terra: The moon is assigned stations until it returns like an old date stalk. This gives a Qur'anic sequence behind the source's crescent and lunar-station details.

luna: The verse says the sun cannot overtake the moon and each moves in an orbit; it gives the two lights distinct bounds rather than divine independence. | terra: The sun does not overtake the moon, night does not outstrip day, and each swims in an orbit. It marks the ordered boundaries among the lights and times that the image holds together.
terra: “Worship Me; this is a straight path” states the positive relation that 27:24 reverses: devotion to something other than Allah turns people away from the path.
terra: Allah is Lord of the heavens, earth, what lies between them, and the easts. It names the celestial totality and horizons as belonging to one Lord.
terra: Allah adorns the lowest heaven with the adornment of stars. It presents the stellar sky as an adornment made by its Lord.

luna: God wraps night over day and day over night and subjects sun and moon to a term; this gives the section’s turning sky its explicit cycle and limit. | terra: Allah wraps night over day and day over night, and subjects sun and moon until an appointed term. It connects the image's daily alternation to the finitude and service of its lights.
terra: Allah makes night for rest and day for sight. Its repeated formulation presents the visible day as a divine favor, not an autonomous light.

luna: The section’s dictionary gloss treats the sky as what stands above and shelters; 40:64 calls it a structure (السماء بناء) above the settled earth, another concrete overhead image. | terra: Allah makes the sky a built structure and identifies Himself as Lord. It gives another concrete Qur'anic form to the source's overhead sama.
terra: Allah adorns the nearest heaven with lamps and assigns it protection. It provides a created-heaven setting for lights that humans must not worship.

luna: The section’s source dictionary notes the sun-name الإلاهة because people worshiped it; 41:37 directly forbids سجود to sun and moon and directs سجود to their Creator, sharpening إياك نعبد. | terra: It gives the section's distinction in an explicit command: do not prostrate to the sun or moon; prostrate to Allah who created them, matching the move from celestial lights to إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ.
luna: In another Abrahamic declaration, he disavows what his father and people worship; it repeats the rejection that the section stages through the setting star, moon, and sun.
luna: Abraham excepts the One who created him and says that He will guide him; this joins the section’s Creator and hidaya themes in a parallel Abrahamic formulation.
terra: Jesus commands worship of Allah, his Lord and theirs, calling it a straight path. It clarifies the positive direction opposite the sun-worshippers' blocked path.

terra: The alternation of night and day is listed among signs for people who understand. It connects the source's daily sequence to discernment in a passage that also looks to what comes from the sky.
terra: People are asked to look at the sky above them—how Allah built and adorned it without fissures. It gives the visible vault in the source an explicitly created form.

luna: The verse tells the Prophet to glorify God before sunrise and before sunset; it places worship of God at the same solar boundaries used to define the section’s daylight. | terra: After commanding patience, the ayah commands praise before sunrise and before sunset. Its two solar edges frame devotion in the same daily span.
luna: The following verse continues glorification through the night and after prostration; it completes the solar-boundary worship in 50:39 with the night side of the cycle.
terra: The command is to prostrate and glorify Allah during the night and at the retreat of the stars. It pairs a setting-star scene with worship directed away from the star.
terra: The oath is by the star when it descends. It closely resembles Abraham's setting-star scene; whether this descent is specifically a setting is interpretively uncertain.

terra: Immediately after the oath by the descending star, the ayah says the Messenger has neither gone astray nor erred. Its own contribution directly joins the star scene to the source's hidayah-and-dalal contrast.
terra: Allah is named as Lord of Sirius. Naming a star's Lord makes a pointed celestial parallel to the source's refusal to treat a visible heavenly light as lord.

luna: الشمس والقمر بحسبان gives the sun and moon an ordered calculation; it complements the section’s measured day and lunar stations. | terra: The sun and moon are by calculation. It reinforces the source's account of a measurable day and the moon's counted stations.

luna: The verse says النجم and trees prostrate; النجم can mean a star or a low-growing plant, so the celestial reading is uncertain, but it would reverse treating a heavenly light as an object of worship.

luna: The section’s q-w-m dictionary includes ميزان النهار standing in balance; 55:7 places the balance (الميزان) alongside the raised sky, giving a Qur’anic counterpart while using balance in its own cosmic measure sense. | terra: Allah raises the sky and sets the balance. It places the image's two linked expressions—an elevated sky and the day's balance becoming upright—side by side without collapsing their distinct meanings.
luna: The verse after the balance is set warns not to transgress it (ألا تطغوا في الميزان); it shows the Quranic measure’s moral use, distinct from the source dictionary’s balanced-noon image.
luna: The next verse commands just weight and not diminishing the balance (وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط); it completes the passage’s move from the section’s day-balance dictionary image to measured justice.
terra: Allah is Lord of the two easts and the two wests. The plural horizons give a celestial extension of the source's sunrise-to-sunset frame.
terra: Allah causes night to enter day and day to enter night, while knowing what is within hearts. It repeats the source's turning day-and-night image with an inward accountability dimension.
terra: Allah adorns the nearest heaven with lamps. The ayah's own depiction of stars as placed lamps supports the source's creature-versus-Creator distinction.
terra: The angels and Spirit ascend to Allah in a day measured as fifty thousand years. This makes the source's day-word extend beyond the sunrise-to-sunset image into an explicitly different scale.
terra: The oath invokes the Lord of the easts and wests. It makes the recurring horizons of the daily sun an aspect of divine lordship.
luna: The verse describes seven heavens layered above (سماوات طباقا); it concretizes the section’s named sky as an encompassing upper sphere.

luna: The verse calls the moon a light and the sun a lamp (نورًا … سراجًا); it gives the image’s two visible lights distinct created roles. | terra: Allah makes the moon a light among the heavens and makes the sun a lamp. Its distinct functions sharpen the source's paired moon-and-sun image.
terra: Allah is Lord of east and west, with no deity but Him, so He is to be taken as guardian. The horizon-pair is explicitly joined to exclusive devotion.

luna: On the Day of Resurrection the moon is darkened (خسف القمر); this is a stated boundary to the ordinary lunar light and stations in the image, and 75:9 joins the sun and moon. | terra: At the final upheaval the moon is darkened. The loss of its light is a boundary against treating the changing moon of the source as divine.

luna: The next verse says the sun and moon are joined (جمع الشمس والقمر) at Resurrection, reversing the distinct courses and stations of the image’s two lights. | terra: The sun and moon are brought together at the final upheaval. Their ordinary ordered separation in the source's sky is reversed, showing both are subject to a greater command.
terra: The Prophet is told to remember his Lord's name morning and evening. It gives the day’s opening and closing light a response parallel to the source's exclusive worship.
terra: People are sent to a three-branched “shade” in the fire scene. It is a severe reversal of the source's overhead shade, since the following ayah denies it gives real shelter.
terra: The following ayah says that this shade is neither cool nor protective from flame. Its own contribution fixes the contrast with a true overhead shade.

luna: The verse says God built seven strong heavens above people (فوقكم سبعا شدادا); this gives the section’s covering sky a layered, built form. | terra: Allah builds seven strong layers above people. Its own contribution is the sky's deliberate overhead construction, which frames the following blazing light.

luna: The verse calls the sun a blazing lamp (سراجا وهاجا), a direct image of the daylight sun that the section distinguishes from God. | terra: The “blazing lamp” is commonly understood as the sun; on that reading, this ayah gives the source's midday light an intense created form. The solar referent is not named in the ayah itself.
terra: Allah raises the heaven's height and proportions it. It supplies the constructed vault whose night and brightness the next ayah describes.
terra: Allah darkens the heaven's night and brings out its brightness. It renders the source's day/night sky as a deliberate alternation in the heaven itself.

luna: At the cosmic end, the sun is rolled up (الشمس كورت); this reverses the ordinary daylight course that the section follows from rising to setting. | terra: The sun is folded up at the final upheaval. The reversal of its daily shining underscores that the solar light is a created, ending sign.

luna: The next verse says the stars grow dim or fall away (النجوم انكدرت); it extends the same end-time reversal to the celestial contents surrounding the section’s sun and moon. | terra: The stars lose their light or fall away at the final upheaval. Against Abraham's setting star, this is the cosmic limit of the same visible lights.
luna: The sky splits open (السماء انفطرت) at the Day of Judgment, reversing the section’s dictionary image of an overhead sheltering sky.

luna: The next verse says the stars scatter (الكواكب انتثرت), extending the sky’s opening to the luminaries contained in the section’s celestial sphere. | terra: The stars are scattered at the final upheaval. It gives a further boundary to the ordinary, navigable stellar sky developed in the source.
terra: The oath by the moon when it becomes full is the lunar boundary opposite the source's newly risen crescent; together they make the moon's changing form perceptible.

luna: The oath by the sun and its brightness (الشمس وضحاها) directly stages the daylight light at the center of this image. | terra: The oath by the sun and its brightness isolates the solar light that fills the section's daytime sky.

luna: The next oath names the moon when it follows the sun (والقمر إذا تلاها); it places the section’s sun and moon in one observed sky sequence. | terra: The moon follows the sun. It gives a concise relation between the two lights in the source's ordered sky.

luna: The next oath names day when it displays the sun (والنهار إذا جلاها); it states the day-and-sun relation that the section develops through sunrise, noon, and sunset. | terra: Day discloses the sun. It directly stages the day as the sun-lit span described in the source.

luna: The following oath names night when it covers the sun (والليل إذا يغشاها), completing the day-to-night arc around the section’s daylight image. | terra: Night covers the sun. Along with the preceding ayat, it makes the daily covering and uncovering of the light explicit.
terra: The oath by the sky and the One who built it completes the surrounding sun, moon, day, and night scenes by naming their overhead setting as made.
terra: The oath by night as it covers repeats the source's visual movement of darkness over the lit sky.
terra: The oath by day as it shines gives the complementary emergence of visible daylight.
terra: The oath by the bright morning gives the dawn-side of the solar day a distinct visual presence.
terra: The still night completes the preceding morning scene with the other side of the daily rhythm.
